preconditions.text: The victim's address is an operator address used to register agent instances.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.
evidence: Neither the `ServiceManager.registerAgents` nor `ServiceRegistry.registerAgents` functions check whether the given instances addresses are already in use as operator address. So if a malicious operator uses another operator's address as an instance address while registering agent instances for a service, it will permanently block the other operator from registering any agent instance for any service in the future.
There are currently operators onchain using same address to register agent instances.

safety.text: An operator must be able to register instances for many services with the same address.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.
evidence: The DOS'ed operators can use another address but this will make managing instances harder for the operators. Plus the design supports registration of multiple/unlimited instances per operator for different services so this feature will be broken. Even worse, the malicious operator can keep registering any new operator address to ensure the DOS.
- The feature where an operator can register instances for many services with the same address is broken.

preconditions.text: An attacker can create a service with many slots for the purpose of the attack.; The service can be created without the intention to push it to deploy, kept at ActiveRegistration state to register instances.; The victim's address is an operator address used to register agent instances.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.
evidence: An attacker can create a service with many slots just for this purpose. This attack cannot be stopped by pausing the `ServiceManager` as there is not pause check in the `ServiceManager.registerAgents` function.

The operator whitelist too is not helpful in this case as it is per service not global. So if the attacker creates his service, the whitelist won't help. The service can be created without the intention to push it to deploy but only to keep it at `ActiveRegistration` state just to be able to register instances and DOS other operators.

safety.text: An operator address must not be usable as an agent instance address while it is in use as an operator address; it may only be used as an instance address after its registered instance count reaches zero.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.
evidence: Add a mapping in `ServiceManager` contract to keep track of all operator addresses so that it will be checked when calling `ServiceManager.registerAgents` if any of the provided instances address is already an operator address. At the end of the function (meaning registration successful), add the operator address to the mapping by mapping it with the number of registered instances. During `ServiceManager.unbond`, reduce the mapped number of registered instances so that when 0, the address can be used as an instance address later.

report_ambiguities_declared: Report does not state whether the attacker must be a registered/whitelisted operator for the target service or how the attacker obtains authorization to register instances.
Report does not specify the exact state transition or prior transaction establishing the victim's operator registration beyond the general claim that operators use addresses to register instances.
The permanent-block outcome is described as a consequence of the missing collision check; the precise revert/error on the victim's later registration is not given.
Whether the attacker's service must be in ActiveRegistration at the moment of registration is implied but not stated as a strict precondition.
formalization_limitations_declared: The permanent-block impact is encoded as a grounded Boolean because the report provides no more specific observable for the DoS outcome.
The operator registered instance count is bound to a cross-contract ServiceManager mapping that does not yet exist in the vulnerable code; binding risk is high.
The impact is a broken feature (liveness/DoS) rather than a value or state mismatch; the V witness is a grounded Boolean for the broken multi-service registration feature.
